task: Consolidate five divergent project-model whitelist checks into one ProjectModelPolicy, resolve each assistant's model once in build_agent (user pick -> own model -> project default -> first allowed) without mutating request/assistant inputs, build supervisor subagent descriptions from built executors, and add parent->child chain and policy table tests.

key_reasoning.reason: New ProjectModelPolicy abstraction replaces ModelAvailabilityService.resolve_requested_model / resolve_model_for_execution / validate_model_for_asset_creation, dependecies.enforce_allowed_model and ToolkitService._ensure_project_allows_model; reshapes AssistantService.build_agent, assistant_engine_builder (create_subagent_executors, builtin clone, descriptions), AssistantFactory, _ask.py pre-resolution, catalog/management routers, plus AIToolsAgent and workflow base_node consumers. Base L (3-4 components with shared utilities) bumped to XL for touching the core shared policy used by every agent builder.

Reviewer gave a concrete 5-point fix and the selection order already exists in pick_allowed_model, but several semantics are open: None-with-default_model handling differs per site, [] is unrestricted in resolve_requested_model but deny-all elsewhere (changing it alters catalog response), whether AIToolsAgent._resolve_llm_model and get_llm_by_credentials re-resolution stay, conversation-override ordering, and whether build_agent_for_workflow gets enforcement. 'Keep current handling' must be pinned per call site.

Closest pattern is pick_allowed_model plus enforce_allowed_model unit tests, which cover selection order but not None/[]/missing-default unification or the non-mutating contract. Seven build_agent callers (handlers, hedged, A2A, health check) rely on current mutation; model_fields_set side effect on request.llm_model; existing tests assert in-place mutation and patch core.dependecies paths. Model whitelist is access enforcement (authz red flag). Mitigated by projectModelOverride flag being off by default. Existing parameterized tests for enforce_allowed_model cover the table-test pattern, so no edge-case bump.

About 10-12 source files modified (model_availability_service, dependecies, toolkit_service, assistant_service, assistant_engine_builder, assistant_factory, _ask.py, catalog.py, management.py, assistant_agent, base_node, llm_service) plus a large share of ~24 test files referencing the policy surface, and 1-3 new files (policy module or tests for chain/table). Spans service, core, router, agents and tests directories.

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from L to XL: touches core shared utilities (project model policy consumed by root, sub-assistants, builtin subagents, agents and workflows); the 'affects multiple workflows or agents' flag describes the same fact and was not applied a second time to avoid inflating to XXL (cross-system), which a single-repo change is not
Technical Risk bumped from M to L: affects authorization-like enforcement (project model whitelist access policy)
